gen-tourney-fs-epilogue: Athletic and loud, Tourney stretches its words wide and bulky. Epilogue is the soft-spoken counterpart, a plain sans with curvy, wire-thin letters that make ordinary text feel approachable.
gen-tourney-fs-merriweather-sans: Tourney stretches its wide-tracked, bulky letters across the line, every stroke cut to one width. And Merriweather Sans follows with tall lowercase and an openly turned e, which makes the words underneath look sturdy and large.
gen-tourney-fs-public-sans: Trustworthy is the first word that comes to mind for Public Sans, and it helps that Tourney shouts above it. Its hefty lowercase and broad c and s openings would keep a long passage steady and comfortable, a plain sans doing quiet work.
gen-press-start-2p-fs-supreme: Press Start 2P spaces its big-bowled lowercase far apart, like cut-out letters pinned to a board. But Supreme keeps things crisp below it, a heavy strip of sans text with letterforms that stay held open.
gen-righteous-general-sans: General Sans keeps a steady pen pressure with an x-height that fills the line. And a longer passage would glide along smoothly, since every bend stays unobstructed, while Righteous, bent like thin steel rod, handles the loud part.
gen-tourney-manrope: Tourney stretches its bulky small letters wide, every stroke cut to a single width. Manrope then brings a bright gap at each curve and a minimal step from capitals down to lowercase, a plain sans that feels instantly friendly.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-fs-epilogue: Edo SZ gives its lowercase the stature of cast iron capitals, with one constant stroke width. Epilogue is the better talker, a sans with curvy, tall-bodied letters and stubby ascender tips that feel unclamped.
gen-dafont-galaxy-fs-asap: Galaxy looks wire-bent across the whole word, its dense tall lowercase loosely spaced out like stars. Asap does the everyday reading work, with open arcs on its c and a body height nearly matching capitals.
gen-almendra-display-fs-paquito: Ornate and literary, Almendra Display lets its letters stay wide open with a pronounced x-height. But Paquito is the one to carry the talking, a confident text serif whose lowercase sits nearly level with its capitals.
gen-audiowide-fs-paquito: Paquito reads confident and approachable, with lowercase that sits almost level with its capitals. And a long page of it would feel friendly and steady, while Audiowide, with no thick-thin shift at all, stays the techy voice up top.
